A_target.statement:
The [[Definition:Sum Type|sum type]] $A + B$ has introduction rules $\mathsf {inl}: A \to A + B$ and $\mathsf {inr}: B \to A + B$, and elimination by case analysis, with:
:$\map {\mathsf {case} } {\map {\mathsf {inl} } a, f, g} \to \map f a$

B_source.statement: [[Definition:Disjunction|Disjunction]] $A \lor B$ is introduced from a proof of $A$ or of $B$, and eliminated by [[Proof by Cases|proof by cases]].

derived.a proof of A or B: a term of type A + B

validity_conditions: The two intro rules of disjunction correspond to the two injections; the elim rule (cases) corresponds to the match eliminator.
The reduction (beta) rule for the eliminator mirrors the proof-normalization step of or-elimination.
So the logical rules of 'or' transport verbatim to the term rules of the sum type.
proof_plan: Map $\lor$-introduction left and right to $\mathsf {inl}$ and $\mathsf {inr}$.
Map $\lor$-elimination, [[Proof by Cases|proof by cases]], to the eliminator $\mathsf {case}$.
Match normalization: a detour introducing $A \lor B$ from $A$ and then eliminating it reduces to the left branch, as $\map {\mathsf {case} } {\map {\mathsf {inl} } a, f, g} \to \map f a$.

Hence the sum type is disjunction under the [[Definition:Curry-Howard Correspondence|Curry-Howard correspondence]].
{{qed}}
